title: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
summary: sin⁻¹x: domain [−1, 1], range [−π/2, π/2]. cos⁻¹x: domain [−1, 1], range [0, π]. tan⁻¹x: domain R, range (−π/2, π/2). cot⁻¹x: range (0, π). sec⁻¹x: domain |x| ≥ 1, range [0, π] − {π/2}. cosec⁻¹x: domain |x| ≥ 1, range [−π/2, π/2] − {0}.
sin⁻¹(−x) = −sin⁻¹x, tan⁻¹(−x) = −tan⁻¹x, cos⁻¹(−x) = π − cos⁻¹x. sin⁻¹x + cos⁻¹x = π/2 and tan⁻¹x + cot⁻¹x = π/2.
tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹y = tan⁻¹[(x + y)/(1 − xy)] (xy < 1). 2tan⁻¹x = tan⁻¹[2x/(1 − x²)].
tan⁻¹(tan θ) = θ only when θ is in (−π/2, π/2); otherwise shift by π. For example tan⁻¹(tan 5π/6) = 5π/6 − π = −π/6.
Put x = sin θ, tan θ etc. and draw a right triangle. Example: cos(sin⁻¹x) = √(1 − x²); cot(cosec⁻¹x) = √(x² − 1); tan⁻¹[(√(1 + x²) − 1)/x] = ½tan⁻¹x (put x = tan θ).

objective: Match: (i) cos⁻¹(½ sin(π/3 + sin⁻¹ ½)); (ii) cos⁻¹(−sin 7π/6). [π/3, 2π/3]

(i) sin⁻¹½ = π/6, so sin(π/3 + π/6) = sin π/2 = 1 ⇒ cos⁻¹(½) = π/3.
(ii) sin 7π/6 = −½ ⇒ −sin 7π/6 = ½ ⇒ cos⁻¹(½) = π/3.
Fill in the blanks: (a) cos⁻¹(½) + 2 sin⁻¹(½) = ______. (b) If cot⁻¹(3/4) = x, then cos x = ______.

(a) π/3 + 2(π/6) = 2π/3.
(b) cot x = 3/4 ⇒ adjacent 3, opposite 4, hypotenuse 5 ⇒ cos x = 3/5.
vsa:
Let sin⁻¹x = θ, so sin θ = x and θ ∈ [−π/2, π/2], where cos θ ≥ 0.
cos θ = √(1 − sin²θ) = √(1 − x²).

or: Let cosec⁻¹x = θ, so cosec θ = x. cot θ = √(cosec²θ − 1) = √(x² − 1) (taking x ≥ 1).

vsa: Express tan⁻¹[(√(1 + x²) − 1)/x], x ≠ 0, in the simplest form.

Put x = tan θ: √(1 + tan²θ) = sec θ.
(sec θ − 1)/tan θ = (1 − cos θ)/sin θ = 2 sin²(θ/2)/(2 sin(θ/2) cos(θ/2)) = tan(θ/2).
So the expression = θ/2 = ½ tan⁻¹x.
cot⁻¹√3 = π/6. cos(tan⁻¹x + π/6) = 0 ⇒ tan⁻¹x + π/6 = π/2 ⇒ tan⁻¹x = π/3 ⇒ x = √3.

Let sin θ = √(1 − x). Then cos θ = √(1 − (1 − x)) = √x.
tan θ = √(1 − x)/√x = √((1 − x)/x).

2tan⁻¹(cos x) = tan⁻¹[2 cos x/(1 − cos²x)] = tan⁻¹[2 cos x/sin²x].
So 2 cos x/sin²x = 2/sin x ⇒ cos x = sin x ⇒ x = π/4.
